coverage.reason: Documentation home; carries the left-rail navigation archetype and entry heading hierarchy.
Representative article route; carries heading hierarchy, code-block treatment, and on-this-page outline.
Second inspected route; exercises same-origin internal linking between two inspected article routes.
Authenticated draft-content route; crawl is unauthenticated so this route was not inspected and must not be claimed as observed.

colors.value: a single desaturated accent reserved for inline code and links; no branded gradient
neutral document surface with a high text-to-background contrast for sustained reading

typography.value: descending heading hierarchy (h1 through h4) with roughly 1.25x step between levels
monospaced code face distinct from body text, used in both inline code and fenced code blocks

spacing.value: consistent vertical rhythm between documentation sections; paragraphs and code blocks share a baseline grid

radii.value: small uniform radius on fenced code blocks and inline code chips

shadows.value: no meaningful elevation; the documentation surface is flat by design

layout.value: persistent left-rail navigation with the article content occupying the remaining width on desktop
on-this-page outline anchored to the article heading hierarchy on desktop, collapsing into the article flow on mobile

components.value: left-rail navigation tree with expandable sections; consistent item order across all inspected routes
fenced code blocks with a copy affordance and horizontal scroll contained within the block
single search entry in the top bar reachable above the fold on all inspected viewports

responsiveFindings.value: the left-rail navigation collapses into an operable drawer on narrow viewports and remains keyboard-reachable
code blocks scroll horizontally inside their own container only, preventing full-page horizontal scroll on mobile

accessibility.value: visible focus outline present on interactive elements including the nav tree, search, and code copy button
article routes carry a single h1 with a descending hierarchy, supporting screen-reader outline navigation

motion.value: minor expand/collapse animation on nav tree sections; no decorative motion

voice.value: concise technical-imperative copy; short instructional sentences aimed at a developer reader

evidence.summary: Documentation home leads with a single h1 and a descending heading hierarchy for section navigation.
Inline code spans use a monospaced face and the desaturated accent color.
Persistent left-rail navigation tree with expandable sections on the documentation home.
Single search input in the top bar reachable above the fold on desktop and mobile.
Left-rail navigation repeats with the same section order observed on the documentation home.
Article leads with a single h1 then h2 and h3 sub-sections in a descending hierarchy.
Fenced code block with a copy affordance, monospaced face, and contained horizontal scroll.
On-this-page outline aside mirrors the article heading hierarchy on desktop.
Vertical spacing between documentation sections follows a consistent baseline grid.
At the mobile breakpoint the left-rail collapses into a drawer, the outline moves into the article flow, and code blocks scroll internally.
Left-rail navigation and same-origin internal link from the install route land here without crossing into a blocked route.
Section rhythm matches the install route, confirming a shared documentation layout.
The draft-content route was blocked and NOT inspected. No claim may rely on having observed authenticated draft content.

limitations: The crawl was unauthenticated; the draft-content route at https://example.com/c2-docs-pilot/admin/drafts was blocked and was NOT inspected, so no claim may rely on having observed it.
Only the home and two getting-started article routes were inspected; no claim may rely on pages outside the inspected set.
No authenticated authoring or admin screen was inspected; the migration covers public documentation surfaces only.
The snapshot is non-mutating; no form submission, search query, or state change was attempted during capture.
